results.evidence: The mark-reviewed command is implemented in cottonwood/cli.py (_run_mark_reviewed). It prints recorded.line(), which is 'lead N: hand review <result>', and returns EXIT_OK. The test test_relevant_review_is_recorded_and_counted runs the exact scenario: direct_candidate lead, relevant, --reviewer founder, --date 2026-11-30, with utc_now pinned. It asserts exit 0, stdout 'lead 1: hand review relevant', one activity of type hand_review, payload == {"result": "relevant", "reviewer": "founder"}, and occurred_at falling on 2026-11-30 in Denver. It also asserts that 'cottonwood report --from 2026-11-30 --to 2026-11-30' contains '- Hand review direct_candidate relevant: 1' and '- Hand review direct_candidate total: 1'. I ran tests/test_mark_reviewed.py and all 17 tests passed.

Without --date, the CLI calls hand_review.parse_review_date(None, events.denver_today()). denver_today() is timeutil.local_date(timeutil.utc_now()), and it looks utc_now up at call time, so a pin works. The day is stored as events._day_start(day), the start of that Denver day. test_date_defaults_to_today_in_denver pins utc_now to 2026-12-01T00:00:00Z, runs mark-reviewed without --date, and asserts local_date(occurred_at) == 2026-11-30. All 17 tests in tests/test_mark_reviewed.py pass.
results.quote:
def test_date_defaults_to_today_in_denver(db_path: Path) -> None:
    lead = _lead(db_path)
    assert _mark(db_path, lead, "irrelevant") == EXIT_OK
    occurred = _activities(db_path)[0]["occurred_at"]
    assert timeutil.local_date(occurred).isoformat() == DAY

results.evidence: test_fabricated_partner_counts_as_a_data_quality_failure creates a relationship_prospect lead and runs mark-reviewed <id> fabricated --reviewer founder --date 2026-11-30. It then runs the report for 2026-11-30 to 2026-11-30 and asserts both required lines are present. The test's lead id comes from lastrowid, not a hard-coded 2, but it is the first lead inserted in a fresh DB, so the id is 1 rather than 2. The id has no bearing on the result. It is used for the five cases: inbound_inquiry lead (stderr contains 'lead: type'), lead 99 (stderr contains 'no lead 99'), reviewer '   ', and --date 2026-02-30 and 2026-12-01 (parametrized; Denver today is 2026-11-30 with utc_now pinned to 2026-12-01T00:00:00Z). results.evidence: Two tests in tests/test_mark_reviewed.py cover this AC, and all 17 tests in the file pass. The first test checks that a second mark-reviewed without --replace exits with the refused code, writes an 'error:' stderr line that contains 'relevant' and 'activity <first_id>', and leaves one activity row. The second test checks that with --replace the exit code is OK, activities are [hand_review, correction, hand_review], the correction's voids_activity_id is the first review's id, the new payload result is irrelevant, and the report shows relevant 0, irrelevant 1 and total 1. Caveats: I did not run the CLI by hand. The test uses the constant EXIT_REFUSED, and I did not confirm that its value is 1. The test also asserts the lead id from the _lead helper, not necessarily id 1.
